content: I will rewrite `src/app/page.tsx` using `write_to_file` with `Overwrite: true` to implement the updated HTML structure, integrate the 6 actual products from their old store, place the brand logo in the header and footer, configure a category filter, and add a fully working WhatsApp checkout system.
thinking:
**Analyzing Code Changes**

Okay, I'm diving into the `src/app/page.tsx` file. My focus is on updating the `PRODUCTS` mock array. I need to ensure it accurately reflects the six products from the old store. The first product I'm updating is "Camiseta Street Logo Off-White", which needs its price set to 120.00 and the image path `/PRODUT...`. I'm starting here to reconstruct the data.


**Updating Product Inventory**

I've completed the data reconstruction for the mock array, including prices and image paths for each product. I've now introduced an `esgotado` (out of stock) property to the `Product` interface. I'll need to implement conditional rendering of an "ESGOTADO" badge and disable the purchase button when this is true. I'm also planning to incorporate the new logo image.

**Implementing Logo Placement**

I'm now integrating the logo into the website's header and footer. I've located the header implementation, and I am placing the logo image adjacent to the brand name "Seu Marquinho" within a flex container. My next step involves adjusting the styling to ensure a visually appealing presentation.


**Structuring the Home Page**

I'm now outlining the structure of the homepage within `src/app/page.tsx`. I have the layout in mind: a navigation bar, a hero section, the Bento brand story, the product grid, a showcase for craftsmanship, a newsletter section, and a footer. It will be a single-page app. I will focus on optimizing image loading and ensure a clean, well-tested implementation.


**Preserving Essential Functionality**

I'm now integrating the existing features into the new UI. I've analyzed the current code base and identified crucial states, functions, and animations that I need to preserve. My priority is to keep the existing cart functionality, search filters, and the "added to cart" popups. I'm focusing on designing product cards that align with the new mockup aesthetics, including square aspect ratios, dark backgrounds, and visual cues for limited or new items. I also plan to incorporate a Framer Motion hover effect for a smooth transition, displaying either "Comprar" or "Ver detalhes". Finally, I've outlined the new grid layout and will add a categories filter above it for a premium look.


**Implementing Category Filtering**

I've crafted a state hook and implemented category tabs using a clean, mockup-consistent design. The selected category filters the product display effectively. I'm now integrating a search query consideration, and I need to ensure the correct image paths for each product are used. I'm double-checking the asset directory for all images. The plan is to completely rewrite `src/app/page.tsx`.


**Drafting the Core Page**

I'm now drafting the `src/app/page.tsx` file, starting with the `use client` directive and necessary imports. I've re-examined the imports, noting that `Instagram` requires an inline SVG. I've begun defining the `PRODUCTS` array with the initial product details and will continue fleshing out the array with further data.


**Defining Product Data**

I'm now focusing on defining the product data. I've added four more product entries to the `PRODUCTS` array, completing the product data. I'm ensuring each product has an ID, name, price, image path, category, a detailed description, and an `esgotado` property where applicable.


**Refining Page Layout**

I'm now integrating the logo, `IMG_3898.PNG`, into the header and footer, after confirming its square display with `object-fit: contain` looks right. I am implementing the custom scrollbar and glassmorphic header as planned. The parallax effects are also in progress. I will be sure that all of the layout components match the HTML mockup.

args.Description: "Update page.tsx to align with the new HTML layout, add brand logo in the header and footer, incorporate 6 actual products from their old store, and implement a WhatsApp-based checkout workflow."
